activeMission: Merged to main and main is green. The two gates that had never completed in this repository -- the mutation war and the real-database suite -- both run to completion with nothing skipped. Every remaining blocker is a credential, an account, an external party or elapsed time. The next thing that moves the north star is one owner-authorized first sprint, not more engineering.

completed: Drove founder-absence softwareGaps from 3 to 0. The two probes that could never be satisfied were repaired rather than deleted: one pointed at code the merge had replaced, and one asked canon to name the commit that contains it.

Fixed a real defect main is shipping: src/proposal-acceptance-engine.mjs set commercialTruthEligible from the proposal's own paymentEvidence.origin, so any caller-supplied "EXTERNAL" string laundered a fixture into payment eligibility. The evidence reference must now survive inspection, and the field is renamed ELIGIBLE_FOR_CANONICAL_PAYMENT_VALIDATION_NOT_CLEARED_REVENUE.

Fixed a second, subtler defect: the canon-drift row and tests/canon-freshness.test.mjs both treated a canon regeneration as evidence of drift -- the doctor because canon cannot name the commit containing it, the test because it counted config/system-readiness-input.json (the generator's own input) as source. Both were permanently red, which is the failure mode that teaches a reader to skip the row.

Repaired the real-database gate, which had never once completed. It ran tests/omnia-v9-external-effect-state-machine, stopped inside it, and waited; roughly 180 tests scheduled after it had never executed and no run said so. Four attempts, each moving the hang one layer up, ended at: bounded per-test timeout, a fresh database per suite, a fixed connection leak, and no cleanup at all -- a disposable embedded server does not need housekeeping, and paying for it with an unbounded DROP DATABASE wait is how a gate stops reporting.

Merged sixteen commits of sol/night-convergence-runtime-harvest-20260902 against nine of newly advanced main. Two collisions resolved by verified semantics, not branch preference: lead-path-sprint-fulfillment.mjs resolved to main's because the branch version reimplemented a parallel state machine instead of composing service-fulfillment.mjs, and Postal resolved to main's evidence layer because this lane's adapter hardening was already present in v1.3.0.

Rebound src/first-cash-canary-packet.mjs to the canonical fulfilment module and rebuilt its canary around proving the canonical machine refuses synthetic payment evidence, rather than simulating a delivery.

Added compileDomainPurposePlan and evaluateDomainObservation (refuses unowned roots and unowned assignment hosts; a generated expectation is not observed proof), single-gateway identity in the model provider doctor, and receipt-derived LIVE routing that refuses caller-supplied state.

Mutation library 138 -> 152, every anchor resolving to exactly one site. POSTAL-QUARANTINE is the finding worth keeping: anchored on the ledger wrapper's quarantine filter it SURVIVED, because deriveCurrentPostalState filters the same three fields immediately afterwards. A redundant guard is unfalsifiable. Re-anchored on the filter that decides, it kills.

tests/omega-closure-hostile.test.mjs: ten attacks on software-gap masking, CODE_READY without observation proof, canary arithmetic, gate conjunction, delivery-machine refusal, unowned domains, generated DNS, credential leaks, LIVE capacity conjuring and canon freshness.

Converged PR #329 (Frontier Operator, Open Model Universe, mutation-registry anchor integrity, owner PayPal.me binding) into this branch. Two lanes had harvested the same night branch and diverged; neither head carried the other's work. Collisions resolved on evidence: this branch's 597-line first-cash implementation over #329's 118, with #329's payment-link semantics absorbed into it, and the mutation registry taken as a set union verified by comparison rather than by reading the diff.

Found and fixed a conflation of my own in the process: WHAT_PAYMENT_LINK answered out of the payment-rail doctor's state, so the packet reported no payment link while the owner had supplied a public one. A destination and a rail are different facts. The link is PREPARED at https://paypal.me/Sarawessam; reconciliation stays EXTERNAL_PROOF_REQUIRED; paymentRailLiveReady stays false and canContact with it. PAYMENT_LINK_IS_NOT_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROOF rides on every packet whether or not a link is present. Non-HTTPS and unparseable links fail closed to null.

PR #329 was red on main's own reachability ratchet before this merge: twelve modules landed implemented, tested, green and unreachable. Classified behind two registered gates rather than wired, because an orchestrator that runs is the last thing to switch on before its consequence path is decided. open-model-runtime-executor is the exception and is already wired, which is why production reachability rose 139 -> 140.

Fixed two provider-list tests that broke on the fifth provider, and they broke differently: one pinned the exact list (updated, not loosened, so adding a provider stays a visible act) and one read the sandbox by array position, finding the wrong row and reporting a defect that did not exist. Verified independently that all five providers fail closed by default.

Made the mutation war find an installed browser. It read CHROMIUM_PATH, nothing sets it, and Chromium is on this host, so it printed SKIPPED_NEEDS_BROWSER for a guard it could exercise while also printing "0 not killed". scripts/resolve-chromium.mjs accepts only executable files, respects a declared install root, and returns nothing rather than a plausible path, so an honest skip survives.

Made the mutation war survive interruption. Four consecutive runs were killed by container restarts, each discarding every verdict earned, so the summary line the readiness artifact quotes had never been produced for the current registry. MUTATION_WAR_JOURNAL appends verdicts as they are decided and replays them, bound to a hash of the file, anchor, replacement and killing suites so a guard that moved runs again rather than inheriting an answer. It proved itself the same session: a restart mid-run cost nothing.

Drove test:mutation-war to 164/164 with nothing skipped. Seven defects came out of the gate itself, each of which had been reporting a guard as untested while printing a clean summary line: it read CHROMIUM_PATH and nothing sets it; SKIPPED_NEEDS_POSTGRES meant nobody had handed the run a database; suites ran with no deadline so one hang stopped everything with no verdict; 160 mutations shared one database and then one server, so the gate measured the order it visited them in; and a hang beside a kill erased the kill.

Made the war resumable after four consecutive runs were lost to container restarts, each discarding every verdict earned. Verdicts are journaled as decided and bound to a hash of the file, anchor, replacement and killing suites, so a guard that moved runs again rather than inheriting an answer. Skips are never journaled, because a skip describes the host rather than the guard.

Drove test:postgres-real to 23 suites / 184 tests / 184 pass. It had never completed: it stopped inside the state-machine suite and waited, so ~180 tests behind that file had never executed and no run said so. Three causes: ~600 client round trips (now four PL/pgSQL statements), a concurrency test that only passed when two transactions happened to overlap (now holds the first transaction open and actually tests FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), and a hundred client-side replays that wedge node:test after ~100 rejected pg queries (now counted server-side).

Established that the replay wedge is the test runner and not production, by measuring four ways before concluding: 200 clean queries in 61ms, conflicts through a pool stopping at ~55 iterations with no backends left, conflicts on one dedicated client stopping at the same ~100, and the identical loop outside node:test doing 300 conflicts in 90ms. No production module was changed for any of it.

Falsified every rewritten check before believing it: claiming all transitions legal fails with Postgres's own message, removing FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED fails the lock test, and dropping UNIQUE from provider_event_id fails the replay test.

Merged 91 commits of main (Fable N+1 orchestration frontier, orchestration graph, no-evaporation startup memory) and reconciled it. Compared failure sets rather than assuming: origin/main fails 24 of its own tests, this branch failed 7, every one of those 7 was also red on main, none was caused by the merge, and this branch repairs 17 that main is shipping red.

Fixed the four inherited non-canon failures: a receipt-ledger fake store missing the add/get pair the ledger requires (the refusal was correct -- a store that cannot refuse a duplicate cannot provide idempotency), a model-admission fixture with no provider that could never have passed (requirement kept, gap given its own test), and a capability count pinned at 8 against a registry holding 11 (updated, not loosened, with the three new supplier ids named individually).
Classified the six frontier proof modules main landed with no entry point, and removed one of my own classifications that main had made false by wiring autonomous-frontier-intelligence.

Merged to main through PRs #354, #359 and #360, and verified main green on a clean worktree afterwards rather than assuming the merge inherited the branch result: 3663 tests, 3608 pass, 0 fail, 55 skipped. Main had 24 failures before this work.

Fixed the last two on main after the first merge: the Playwright crawler fell through to Playwright's own default browser path, which names the exact build its package was published against, so it failed on a host carrying a different build while a working browser sat beside it; and canon named a commit three source files behind, because a regeneration had been committed together with source changes. A regeneration is now its own commit, which is what makes the freshness rule exact.

capabilityGenome.reproduce: npm run capabilities:genome:normalize -- --execute (with UBERBOND_CAPABILITY_GENOME_NETWORK_READS=1). Re-reads the same pinned commits and blobs; a changed body fails the identity check instead of normalizing something else under the same name.
capabilityGenome.whatNormalizationIs: A typed description of an untrusted public document. src/capability-genome-body-normalize.mjs maps prose onto atoms only through the reviewed table in artifacts/capability-genome/atom-evidence-terms.json, takes sideEffectClass from the taxonomy rather than the body, recognises only explicit SPDX licence identifiers, and walks DISCOVERED -> NORMALIZED through transitionCapability so the state has a real history entry.
capabilityGenome.whatTheTwoRecordsActuallySay: anthropics/skills brand-guidelines matched NO atom in the 25-atom taxonomy and normalized with zero atoms, which is a result rather than a failure. vercel-labs/skills find-skills claims exactly one atom, capability.discover, and screens REVIEW for remote-package-execution and unconfirmed-global-install. Both carry license UNKNOWN.
capabilityGenome.securityScreening: Normalization emits STATIC evidence and nothing else. admitCapability requires STATIC, SEMANTIC and SANDBOX, so one regex pass cannot make anything eligible. Screening is bound to the exact content hash it ran against; a quarantined body is still recorded rather than hidden.
capabilityGenome.scannerRepair: The instruction scanner matched `.sh` anywhere in a URL, so a body was flagged HIGH for citing skills.sh while `npx skills add -g -y` -- remote package execution plus a global install with confirmation suppressed -- tripped nothing. The URL rule now requires the extension after the host (path, query or fragment), and two new codes catch the real act. find-skills is still REVIEW, now for the true reason.
capabilityGenome.notClaimed: Two normalized records is two typed descriptions. Nothing is deduped, security-reviewed, eligible, approved, active, installed, benchmarked or economically proven. A skill body is not a capability; NORMALIZED is not APPROVED; STATIC_CLEAR is not SAFE.

knownSuiteIsolationFinding.test: tests/omnia-v9-gmail-effect-adapter-dispatch-recovery.test.mjs -- 'two concurrent recovery workers on the same stuck Gmail-bound execution converge on exactly one outcome'
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.observed: 177/178 once, while test:deterministic, test:browser and test:postgres-real were deliberately pointed at one shared long-lived PostgreSQL.
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.isolatedResult: 178/178 when the suite runs alone. The identical contention on unmodified main also passed 178/178.
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.rootCause: Cross-test interference in a shared table. Three test files call recoverUnresolvedExecutions against omnia_v9_external_effect_executions with limits of 1000, 500 and 50, and node --test runs files in parallel, so a sweep from another file can claim this test's row before either of its own two workers reach it.
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.whyNotABothClaimedDefect: claimUnresolvedForRecovery uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED inside a transaction, so two concurrent workers cannot receive the same row. The 'both claimed' branch is excluded by PostgreSQL semantics, which leaves 'neither' as the only way the assertion can fail.
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.notCausedByThisShift: No module changed in this shift appears anywhere in that test's 12-module import graph.
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.notFixed: The test was left alone rather than weakened. The real fix is test-level isolation -- the disposable per-run database the suite's own comments already name as its convention -- not a filter added to production recovery code to suit tests.
knownSuiteIsolationFinding.reproduce: Run test:deterministic, test:browser and test:postgres-real concurrently against one OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL.
